source.title: Learning with Noisy Labels for Sentence-level Sentiment Classification
source.authors: Hao Wang; Bing Liu; Chao-Zhuo Li; Yan Yang; Tian-Rui Li

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the effect of increasing label corruption on clean-test accuracy in sentence-level sentiment classification, a new modality and setting; it does not report training error.
record.gate_note: Experiment 1 reports clean-test accuracy across corruption rates in Figure 2. The paper does not report training error for these models. Cited results about memorization from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: Experiment 1 tests the test-error component of V4 in sentence sentiment classification: CNN clean-test accuracy declines as randomly flipped training labels increase. It does not measure fitting or memorization of those labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes Experiment 1. The paper's broader conclusion is that alternating two CNN networks with learned noise transitions improves sentiment classification under noisy supervision, generally outperforming the tested baselines.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses CNNs for sentence-level sentiment classification and randomly flips labels in clean-labeled training sets; it reports clean-test accuracy, not training error on fully random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise rate; dataset (Movie, Laptop, Restaurant); model (CNN, NETAB).

fits_no_version.finding: NETAB outperforms CNN under synthetic label noise and generally outperforms comparison methods on real noisy training data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A noise-aware training method improves clean-test sentiment classification performance under noisy supervision.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The relevant accuracy results are presented only in Figure 2, without numeric values or uncertainty estimates in the text. Training-set error is not reported, so the paper cannot establish whether the models fit the corrupted training labels.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: Figure 2 is the only source for the Experiment 1 accuracy values, and the text provides no numeric values to record. The text describes the aggregate trend across the three datasets but does not give separate dataset values.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test performance after fitting, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence speed under increasing label corruption.
Fitting shuffled, independently permuted, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training-set fitting throughout corruption, direct evidence of memorizing noise while capturing signal, and the full corruption range. Binary label-flip rates stop at 0.5; flipping every label would invert labels rather than randomize them.
Effects of adding or removing explicit regularization on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning real-label patterns before noisy labels. This property motivates early pretraining but is not measured.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 2 results are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing. Exact per-model, per-dataset values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text. The paper uses V6 as a methodological premise without independently testing it.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test fitting completely random training labels or report training error and test error at chance.
No training time or convergence-speed comparison across corruption rates is reported.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs are tested.

The paper varies the fraction of randomly flipped labels and reports clean-test accuracy, but does not report training error or whether the networks fit each training set perfectly. Figure 2 gives the accuracy values only as plots.
The paper does not test whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation affect fitting random labels or generalization on true labels.
The paper does not measure the order in which networks learn real-label patterns and memorize noisy labels.

relationships.condition: CNN sentence sentiment classification on Movie, Laptop, and Restaurant; random label-flip rates 0–0.5; clean-test accuracy component only.
relationships.reason: Based on Experiment 1 text and Figure 2, with no extracted row ids: accuracy declines as corruption increases, summarized as approximately 0.8 to 0.5. This supports the reported degradation trend; training-set fitting remains untested.
relationships.display_finding: Clean test accuracy declined with increasing corruption across Movie, Laptop, and Restaurant, summarized as approximately 0.8 to 0.5.
